title: Separating recycling from general waste on the route
audience: Cleaners on sites that separate general waste from recycling.
learningOutcomes: Set up a two-stream collection and keep each stream pure from desk to drop point.
Decide where an unclear item belongs by checking the site guide rather than guessing.
Handle recycling bags so they are tied, separated and delivered to the right point.

instruction.heading: Two streams, two containers
instruction.body: Where a site separates recycling, the route uses two collection bins that travel together: one for general waste and one for recyclables. Match the colour and label of each bin to the site's signs. Keep each stream pure, because a single wrong item can make a whole recycling load unacceptable to the recycler.

instruction.heading: Sorting at the desk
instruction.body: Empty each desk bin into the stream that matches each item. If you are unsure where an item belongs, check the site guide or ask the site contact. If it is still unclear, place the item in general waste rather than guessing. Do not tip recyclables and general waste into one bag to save a trip.

instruction.heading: Items that cause contamination
instruction.body: Some items spoil recycling even when they are recyclable in principle. Food residue on paper and card is the most common example. Follow the site guide for what counts as acceptable. Keep recycling bags apart on the drop sheet, label them if the site asks, and do not mix the contents when moving them to the outside bin.

procedure: Confirm both streams, their bins and their labels against the site guide.
Empty each desk bin into the matching stream.
Check any unclear item against the guide, and default to general waste if still unsure.
Tie off and mark recycling bags separately from general waste.
Deliver each bag to its own designated point.

workedExamples.situation: A desk bin holds a greasy pizza box and a clean plastic bottle.
workedExamples.reasoning: The site guide decides the bottle. If the site accepts it, it goes to recycling, after any rinsing the guide asks for. The greasy box usually goes to general waste, because food residue on card spoils a recycling load. Check the guide before the route starts rather than deciding during it.

equipmentAndPpe: Two collection bins with matching labels

commonErrors.error: Mixing both streams into one bag to save a trip.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep two bags and two drop points for the route.

commonErrors.error: Guessing at items that are not clearly recyclable.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the site guide. If still unsure, use general waste.

commonErrors.error: Leaving recycling bags at the drop point without counting them.
commonErrors.prevention: Count the bags at the drop point against the route before closing.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Recycling bags can hold broken glass or sharp tins. Wear gloves and secure the bag before moving it.

qualityStandard: Each stream stays separate from desk to drop point.
Recycling bags are tied and labelled as the site requires.
documentationEvidence: Recycling collection recorded against the site collection schedule.
summary: Keep recycling and general waste in separate bags from desk to drop point.
Check the site guide for unclear items; default to general waste if still unsure.
Count and label bags at the drop point before the route closes.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why keep general waste and recycling separate on the route?
options: Because one wrong item can spoil a whole recycling load
So the two bins look tidy in the corridor and easy to find
So the bags are heavier to carry and harder to lift in one go

knowledgeChecks.question: You are unsure whether a desk item is recyclable. What do you do?
options: Check the site guide or ask the site contact, and if still unsure, use general waste
Put it in recycling so it is not wasted and the site will sort it later
Mix it into whichever bag is nearly full and it is quicker than sorting
